leo.intro: I’m Leo. I run a trucking company, and my family lives near the Great Lakes. What would you like to know?

work.text: I founded Leo Trucking Company. Our long-haul trucks drive themselves, and people handle the last mile. I have a BA, but I give experience and an entrepreneurial spirit more credit for my success. I also own a nonprofit that supplies automated medical equipment to underserved communities.

home.text: My wife and I have a large mixed family, and we live near the Great Lakes. The climate, fresh water, and central location for the business all helped us choose it. We love boating, too. We have staff at home and a personal assistant who handles the day-to-day things.

health.text: Wealth is health, as I like to say. I can afford a mobile doctor, personalized healthcare, steak, and access to private places to exercise. That kind of access is a commodity few people can readily afford.

tech.text: I can afford to be less dependent on things like health-tracking wearables, and that is my choice. I still use plenty of automation. My business uses driverless cargo shipping, and drones can deliver food and goods to my boat.

third.text: I spend as much time as I can on my boat on the nearby lakes. I also enjoy hiking in state-reserved and privately owned recreation areas near my home.

sophia.intro: I’m Sophia. I work as a robotic assisted paramedic around rural Wyoming. You can ask about my work or what life looks like outside it.

work.text: I trained at a local technical school to become a robotic assisted paramedic. I serve rural areas in and around Wyoming. My income falls in the low-to-middle range.

home.text: My partner and I rent our home. We hope to buy a place we can stay in for good. I’m also exploring the possibility of having a family, although I’m not sure I can afford children.

health.text: I like locally grown and made food from the farmers market. I would love to grow more of my own if I had the time. Yoga keeps me active, and I use legalized psychedelics.

tech.text: Robotics, automation, and technology are central to my work in healthcare. I wish I could help more people. In my own life, I have a phone, laptop, and a bio-tracker that helps me save on health insurance.

third.text: My community includes the farmers market, the yoga studio, and the rural area where I live. Those are my third spaces outside work and home.

ken.intro: I’m Ken. I’m a Marine logistics specialist and a dad. My son and I live on base in Hawaii. What would you like to ask?

work.text: I’m an enlisted logistics specialist in the Marines, working with an advanced-manufacturing materials warehouse. The military helped me earn my associate’s degree. My income is fixed military pay.

home.text: My five-year-old son and I live in military housing on base in Hawaii. I take being his father seriously, and my service helps give us a foundation. Childcare coverage can be difficult. I left the Marshall Islands as a child, so the thought of being displaced again worries me.

health.text: We try to eat well, but convenience matters when I’m looking after my son. We rely on base food services and supplement them with fast food.

tech.text: Technology is at the center of most of my logistics work. Personally, I have a phone, a computer, and a bio-tracker issued by the Marines.

third.text: There isn’t much time for a third space when you’re a single dad in the service. We get to the beach whenever we can. That’s where I met Leo when he was on vacation in Hawaii.

veronica.intro: I’m Veronica. I’m in seventh grade, and I’m into soccer, gardening, robotics, and gaming. What do you want to explore?

work.text: I attend a small satellite schoolhouse connected virtually to the wider school district. That lets me learn in a rural area while using the resources of a bigger district. My parents support me, and I also have an allowance.

home.text: I live in a stable home about 90 minutes from a major city. I have friends I see in person and friends I meet virtually. I look up to science advocates and hope to work on plant-based renewable diets someday.

health.text: I eat vegetables from our garden and meals delivered around my family’s nutritional needs. Soccer, gardening, robotics, gaming, and volunteering are some of my hobbies.

tech.text: I use a bio-tracker, phone, tablet, and computer, along with smart in-home health and virtual community tools. I also use VR for entertainment and gaming.

third.text: I play soccer, spend time with friends online and in person, and take Catherine’s online gardening classes. I also volunteer for Leo’s nonprofit, which brings medical robotics and technology to underserved communities.

catherine.intro: I’m Catherine. I’m a retired nurse, and gardening and volunteering are important parts of my life now. What would you like to talk about?

work.text: I’m retired after more than 20 years as a registered nurse. I have a full pension and fixed retirement income through my 401K.

home.text: I lost my husband to COVID and now live alone. I worry about who will care for me as I get older. Friends and neighbors have helped me find a community.

health.text: I grow vegetables in my outdoor garden and a smaller one indoors. I also get personalized meals based on my nutritional needs. Gardening and volunteering keep me active and fulfilled. My hearing is waning, and I have had a knee replacement.

tech.text: My wearable is tied to my healthcare. I also use a virtual AI assistant, smart in-home health, virtual community tools, and VR for travel and entertainment.

third.text: I spend time with lifelong friends nearby and have made more connections with younger people in the community. I enjoy community gardening, volunteering, virtual travel, VR entertainment, and time with the local community.
